subject: math
title: Grade 1 Addition and Subtraction to 20
seo_title: Grade 1 Addition and Subtraction to 20 Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Addition and subtraction to 20 (understanding of operation and process)
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on addition and subtraction to 20 for the BC curriculum: add with pictures and ten frames, take away, count on and back on a number line, doubles, near doubles and fact families. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: Adding puts groups together. Subtracting takes some away. Count on from the bigger number.
key_sub: 8 + 3: say 9, 10, 11 (not 8). 6 + 7 is double 6 and 1 more: 13. If 8 + 5 = 13, then 13 − 5 = 8.
body_html:
Add: put groups together

To add, put two groups together. Then find how many in all.

A ten frame helps. Fill the top frame first. A full frame is 10.

Example

What is 9 + 4?

9 + 1 = 10. 3 are left. 10 + 3 = 13.

Answer: 13

Subtract: take away

To subtract, start with a group. Take some away. Count what is left.

Count on and count back

To add a small number, start at the big number. Count on. To take away a small number, count back. Do not say the start number.

Example

What is 14 − 3?

Start at 14. Count back 3: 13, 12, 11.

Answer: 11

Doubles and near doubles

A double adds a number to itself: 6 + 6 = 12. A near double uses two numbers that are 1 apart. Use the double. Then add 1.

DoubleNear double
3 + 3 = 63 + 4 = 7
5 + 5 = 105 + 6 = 11
7 + 7 = 147 + 8 = 15
9 + 9 = 189 + 10 = 19

Fact families

Three numbers make a fact family. If you know 8 + 5 = 13, you know 3 more facts.

Example

What is 12 − 9?

Think: 9 + ? = 12. Count up: 10, 11, 12. That is 3.

Answer: 3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
8 + 3 = 10 (saying 8, 9, 10)Do not say the start number. Say 9, 10, 11. So 8 + 3 = 11.
12 − 5 = 17That adds. “Take away” means subtract. 12 − 5 = 7.
7 + 8 = 147 + 7 = 14. 8 is 1 more, so 7 + 8 = 15.
2 + 9: counting on 9 from 2Start with the bigger number. Say 10, 11. So 2 + 9 = 11.

faq.q: What does Grade 1 math in BC expect for addition and subtraction?
faq.a: The BC Grade 1 curriculum lists addition and subtraction to 20 under Computational fluency. Students learn what adding and taking away mean, and use pictures, ten frames and number lines to solve facts to 20.

faq.q: What strategies help Grade 1 students add and subtract to 20?
faq.a: Useful strategies are counting on from the bigger number, counting back, filling a ten frame to make 10, doubles and near doubles (6 + 7 is double 6 and 1 more), and using fact families.

faq.q: Why is my child’s answer 1 off when counting on?
faq.a: They are usually saying the start number as the first count, like “8, 9, 10” for 8 + 3. Have them hold the 8 in their head and count the jumps: 9, 10, 11.

faq.q: What is a fact family in Grade 1?
faq.a: A fact family is a set of facts that use the same three numbers. For 8, 5 and 13: 8 + 5 = 13, 5 + 8 = 13, 13 − 5 = 8 and 13 − 8 = 5.

sets.title: Add with pictures and ten frames

items.q: 3 apples and 4 more. How many in all?
5 beads and 3 more. How many in all?
items.e: Count on from 5: 6, 7, 8. 5 + 3 = 8.

items.q: 2 salmon and 6 more. How many in all?
6 pucks and 4 more. How many in all?
7 shells and 2 more. How many in all?
items.e: Count on from 7: 8, 9. 7 + 2 = 9.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 9 + 2?
items.e: The top frame has 10. 1 is in the bottom frame. 10 + 1 = 11.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 8 + 4?
items.e: The top frame has 10. 2 are in the bottom frame. 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 7 + 6?
items.e: The top frame has 10. 3 are in the bottom frame. 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 6 + 5?
items.e: The top frame has 10. 1 is in the bottom frame. 10 + 1 = 11.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 8 + 6?
items.e: The top frame has 10. 4 are in the bottom frame. 10 + 4 = 14.

items.q: Fill the top frame first. What is 9 + 7?
items.e: The top frame has 10. 6 are in the bottom frame. 10 + 6 = 16.

items.q: How many more make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes. There are 3. 7 + 3 = 10. So 3 more.

items.q: How many more make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes. There are 6. 4 + 6 = 10. So 6 more.

items.q: How many more make 10?
items.e: Count the empty boxes. There are 2. 8 + 2 = 10. So 2 more.

items.q: The top frame is full. What is 10 + 5?
items.e: A full frame is 10. 10 and 5 more is 15.

items.q: The top frame is full. What is 10 + 8?
items.e: A full frame is 10. 10 and 8 more is 18.

items.q: There are 6 red and 7 blue. Which one matches?
items.e: 6 red and 7 blue make 13 in all. 6 + 7 = 13.

items.q: 5 + 9 = 14. What is 9 + 5?
items.e: You can add in any order. The total stays the same. 9 + 5 = 14.

items.q: What is 4 + 6 + 3?
Ryan counts 8 + 3. He says “8, 9, 10.” What is the right answer?
items.e: Do not say the 8 again. Say 9, 10, 11. So 8 + 3 = 11.

items.q: There are 7. 3 are crossed out. How many are left?
items.e: Take away 3. Count the ones with no X. 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: There are 9. 4 are crossed out. How many are left?
items.e: Take away 4. Count the ones with no X. 9 − 4 = 5.

items.q: There are 8. 5 are crossed out. How many are left?
items.e: Take away 5. Count the ones with no X. 8 − 5 = 3.

items.q: There are 11. 2 are crossed out. How many are left?
items.e: Take away 2. Count the ones with no X. 11 − 2 = 9.

items.q: There are 12. 5 are crossed out. How many are left?
items.e: Take away 5. Count the ones with no X. 12 − 5 = 7.

items.q: There are 15. 4 are crossed out. How many are left?
items.e: Take away 4. Count the ones with no X. 15 − 4 = 11.

items.q: What is 10 − 3?
items.e: 10 counters. 3 have an X. 7 are left.

items.q: What is 8 − 2?
items.e: 8 counters. 2 have an X. 6 are left.

items.q: What is 6 − 5?
items.e: 6 counters. 5 have an X. 1 is left.

items.q: What is 13 − 3?
items.e: Start with 13. Take away 3. Count what is left: 10.

items.q: What is 16 − 4?
items.e: Start with 16. Take away 4. Count what is left: 12.

items.q: What is 14 − 5?
items.e: Start with 14. Take away 5. Count what is left: 9.

items.q: What is 12 − 9?
items.e: Start with 12. Take away 9. Count what is left: 3.

items.q: What is 17 − 8?
items.e: Start with 17. Take away 8. Count what is left: 9.

items.q: What is 20 − 7?
items.e: Start with 20. Take away 7. Count what is left: 13.

items.q: Which one matches the picture?
items.e: There are 11. 4 are crossed out. 7 are left. 11 − 4 = 7.

items.q: Ava sees 12 − 5. She says 17. What is right?
items.e: 17 is 12 + 5. Ava added. Take away 5 from 12. 12 − 5 = 7.

items.q: There were 12. Now 8 are left. How many were taken away?
items.e: Count the ones with an X. 12 − 4 = 8. So 4 were taken away.

items.q: What is 15 − 9?
items.e: Take away 5 from the bottom. Then 4 from the top. 6 are left. 15 − 9 = 6.

items.q: What is 18 − 6?
items.e: 18 cars. 6 have an X. Count the rest: 12.

sets.title: Count on and count back on a number line

items.q: Start at 7. Count on 3. What is 7 + 3?
items.e: Start at 7. Say 8, 9, 10. You land on 10. (Do not count the 7.)

items.q: Start at 11. Count on 4. What is 11 + 4?
items.e: Start at 11. Say 12, 13, 14, 15. You land on 15. (Do not count the 11.)

items.q: Start at 5. Count on 3. What is 5 + 3?
items.e: Start at 5. Say 6, 7, 8. You land on 8. (Do not count the 5.)

items.q: Start at 14. Count on 2. What is 14 + 2?
items.e: Start at 14. Say 15, 16. You land on 16. (Do not count the 14.)

items.q: Start at 16. Count on 3. What is 16 + 3?
items.e: Start at 16. Say 17, 18, 19. You land on 19. (Do not count the 16.)

items.q: Start at 10. Count on 4. What is 10 + 4?
items.e: Start at 10. Say 11, 12, 13, 14. You land on 14. (Do not count the 10.)

items.q: Start at 12. Count back 3. What is 12 − 3?
items.e: Start at 12. Say 11, 10, 9. You land on 9. (Do not count the 12.)

items.q: Start at 15. Count back 4. What is 15 − 4?
items.e: Start at 15. Say 14, 13, 12, 11. You land on 11. (Do not count the 15.)

items.q: Start at 18. Count back 2. What is 18 − 2?
items.e: Start at 18. Say 17, 16. You land on 16. (Do not count the 18.)

items.q: Start at 10. Count back 3. What is 10 − 3?
items.e: Start at 10. Say 9, 8, 7. You land on 7. (Do not count the 10.)

items.q: Start at 19. Count back 4. What is 19 − 4?
items.e: Start at 19. Say 18, 17, 16, 15. You land on 15. (Do not count the 19.)

items.q: Start at 13. Count back 2. What is 13 − 2?
items.e: Start at 13. Say 12, 11. You land on 11. (Do not count the 13.)

items.q: Which one matches the jumps?
items.e: Start at 9. There are 4 jumps to the right. That is adding: 9 + 4 = 13.

items.q: Which one matches the jumps?
items.e: Start at 17. There are 3 jumps to the left. That is taking away: 17 − 3 = 14.

items.q: Start with the bigger number. What is 3 + 8?
items.e: Start at 8, not 3. Count on 3: 9, 10, 11. So 3 + 8 = 11.

items.q: Start with the bigger number. What is 2 + 13?
items.e: Start at 13, not 2. Count on 2: 14, 15. So 2 + 13 = 15.

items.q: Owen counts on for 6 + 3. He says “6, 7, 8.” What went wrong?
items.e: Do not say the start number. Start at 6. Say 7, 8, 9. He said 6 too. 6 + 3 = 9.

items.q: Nadia counts back for 14 − 2. She says “14, 13.” What went wrong?
items.e: Do not say the start number. Start at 14. Say 13, 12. She said 14 too. 14 − 2 = 12.

items.q: How many jumps from 12 to 17?
items.e: Count the jumps, not the numbers: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17. That is 5 jumps. So 12 + 5 = 17.

items.q: How many jumps back from 20 to 17?
items.e: Count the jumps: 19, 18, 17. That is 3 jumps. So 20 − 3 = 17.

items.q: Each frame has 2. What is 2 + 2?
items.e: Both frames have 2. This is a double. 2 + 2 = 4.

items.q: Each frame has 4. What is 4 + 4?
items.e: Both frames have 4. This is a double. 4 + 4 = 8.

items.q: Each frame has 6. What is 6 + 6?
items.e: Both frames have 6. This is a double. 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: Each frame has 9. What is 9 + 9?
items.e: Both frames have 9. This is a double. 9 + 9 = 18.

items.q: Each frame has 10. What is 10 + 10?
items.e: Both frames have 10. This is a double. 10 + 10 = 20.

items.q: Each row has 3 apples. What is double 3?
items.e: Double 3 means 3 + 3. 3 + 3 = 6.

items.q: Each row has 5 apples. What is double 5?
items.e: Double 5 means 5 + 5. 5 + 5 = 10.

items.q: Each row has 8 apples. What is double 8?
items.e: Double 8 means 8 + 8. 8 + 8 = 16.

items.q: Use double 3. What is 3 + 4?
items.e: Double 3 is 6. The blue counter is 1 more. 6 + 1 = 7.

items.q: Use double 5. What is 5 + 6?
items.e: Double 5 is 10. The blue counter is 1 more. 10 + 1 = 11.

items.q: Use double 6. What is 6 + 7?
items.e: Double 6 is 12. The blue counter is 1 more. 12 + 1 = 13.

items.q: Use double 8. What is 8 + 9?
items.e: Double 8 is 16. The blue counter is 1 more. 16 + 1 = 17.

items.q: Use double 9. What is 9 + 10?
items.e: Double 9 is 18. The blue counter is 1 more. 18 + 1 = 19.

items.q: What is 8 + 7?
items.e: Double 7 is 14. 8 is 1 more than 7. 14 + 1 = 15.

items.q: Which one is a double?
items.e: A double adds a number to itself. 7 + 7 is a double.

items.q: Which one is a near double?
items.e: A near double uses two numbers that are 1 apart. 4 and 5 are 1 apart. So 4 + 5 is a near double.

items.q: Double what number makes 16?
items.e: 8 + 8 = 16. So double 8 makes 16. (16 is the total.)

items.q: Arjun says 7 + 8 = 14. What did he forget?
items.e: 7 + 7 = 14. But 8 is 1 more than 7. So 7 + 8 = 14 + 1 = 15. Arjun forgot to add 1.

items.q: Double 7 is 14. What is 14 − 7?
items.e: 7 + 7 = 14. So 14 − 7 = 7. (21 adds instead of taking away.)

items.q: 5 + 6 = 11. What is 6 + 5?
items.e: Same numbers, other order. The total is the same. 6 + 5 = 11.

items.q: Which fact is in this family?
items.e: This family uses 8, 5 and 13. 13 − 5 = 8 uses all three.

items.q: 7 + 4 = 11. Which is the turn-around fact?
items.e: A turn-around fact adds the same numbers in the other order: 4 + 7 = 11.

items.q: Which fact is NOT in this family?
items.e: The family uses 6, 9 and 15. 9 − 6 = 3 does not use 15.

items.q: Which subtraction goes with 9 + 8 = 17?
items.e: Start with the whole, 17. Take away a part, 8. 17 − 8 = 9.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: Think: ? + 5 = 12. 7 + 5 = 12. So the missing part is 7.

items.q: What is the missing part?
items.e: Think: 6 + ? = 14. 6 + 8 = 14. So the missing part is 8.

items.q: How many facts are in the family of 9, 3 and 12?
Kai sees 9 salmon in the creek. 4 more swim in. How many salmon now?
8 cars wait for the ferry. 7 more come. How many cars now?
items.e: Near double. Double 7 is 14. 1 more is 15.

items.q: Olivia finds 14 shells at the beach. She gives 6 to Lucas. How many does she have now?
items.e: Take away 6. 14 − 6 = 8. Check: 8 + 6 = 14.

items.q: 7 bald eagles sit in a cedar tree. 2 fly away. How many are still in the tree?
items.e: Count back 2: 6, 5. So 5 are still there. 7 − 2 = 5.

items.q: It rains in Vancouver on 6 days. Then it rains on 6 more days. How many rainy days?
items.e: This is a double. 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: Mei walks 5 laps in the Terry Fox Run. Wei walks 9 laps. How many more laps does Wei walk?
items.e: Count up from 5 to 9: 6, 7, 8, 9. That is 4. Check: 5 + 4 = 9.

items.q: Some orcas swim by. Then 3 more come. Now there are 10. How many came first?
items.e: Think: ? + 3 = 10. 7 + 3 = 10. So 7 came first.

items.q: Noah has 15 hockey cards. He wants 20. How many more does he need?
13 people ride the SkyTrain. 4 get off. How many are still on?
items.e: 13 − 3 = 10. Take away 1 more: 9. Check: 9 + 4 = 13.

items.q: Jasleen’s class has 10 students on a hike. 6 more join. How many students now?
Simran picks 17 apples in the Okanagan. 8 are red. The rest are green. How many are green?
items.e: Think: 8 + ? = 17. 8 + 9 = 17. So 9 are green.

items.q: 10 children play soccer at recess. 3 go inside. Then 4 come out. How many play now?
items.e: Step 1: 10 − 3 = 7. Step 2: 7 + 4 = 11. (7 stops after step 1.)

items.q: Harjot says 7 + 9 = 16. Which fact checks it?
items.e: Take one part away from the whole. 16 − 9 = 7, so Harjot is right.
